title: Exploring State-Space Models for Data-Specific Neural Representations
claim: A simple encoder-decoder baseline with a state-space block in front of the encoder compresses an input into a small embedding and reconstructs it.
layout: 1 panel, left-to-right, braces labelling encoder and decoder, tensor shapes under blocks
description: A single horizontal pipeline reads left to right. A small blurry input image (3,32,32) feeds a tall purple vertical block labeled 'SSM block'. That block feeds a yellow trapezoid labeled Conv(3,8,8,8) that narrows down to a small green vertical stack of cells, the image embedding (8,4,4). A second yellow trapezoid labeled ConvTranspose(8,3,8,8) widens back out into a reconstructed image (3,32,32) that looks nearly identical to the input. Curly braces above the figure mark 'Encoder' over the SSM and Conv blocks, and 'Decoder' over the ConvTranspose block. Italic captions with tensor dimensions sit under the images and the embedding. Black arrows connect the stages. Pastel yellow, purple and green fills contrast with the photos, and the eye goes first to the colored blocks in the center.
caption: Baseline architecture incorporating SSMs for image reconstruction
abstract: This paper studies the problem of data-specific neural representations, aiming for compact, flexible, and modality-agnostic storage of individual visual data using neural networks. Our approach considers a visual datum as a set of discrete observations of an underlying continuous signal, thus requiring models capable of capturing the inherent structure of the signal. For this purpose, we investigate state-space models (SSMs), which are well-suited for modeling latent signal dynamics. We first explore the appealing properties of SSMs for data-specific neural representation and then present a novel framework that integrates SSMs into the representation pipeline. The proposed framework achieved compact representations and strong reconstruction performance across a range of visual data formats, suggesting the potential of SSMs for data-specific neural representations.
